diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\matM$ and $\matM'$ be of equal size. The rings $\KM$ and ${\mathbb{K}}_{\matM'}$ are isomorphic if their realness is the same.
The {\em realness} of $\KM$ or $\matM$ is the number of real rows in $\matM$.

issues.failure_explanation: The realness ranges over all integers in $\{0,\dots,n\}$ having the parity of $n$ (complex rows come in conjugate pairs), which gives $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1$ values, not $\lceil n/2 \rceil$. For even $n$ the stated formula is off by one: e.g., for $n=2$ the realness can be $0$ or $2$, giving two non-isomorphic tubal rings ($\mathbb{K}_{2,0}\cong\C$ and $\mathbb{K}_{2,2}\cong\R\times\R$, the split-complex numbers), but $\lceil 2/2 \rceil = 1$.

failure_location.quote: Since complex rows in $\matM$ come in pairs, the parity of the realness must be equal to the parity of $n$, thus there are, up to isomorphism, $\lceil \nicefrac{n}{2} \rceil$ tubal rings.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\lceil n/2 \rceil$ by $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1$, the number of integers between $0$ and $n$ whose parity matches $n$.
issues.overall_effect: Only the counting remark is wrong. The isomorphism classification by realness (prop:realness-iso) and all formal results are unaffected; nothing depends on the erroneous count.
issues.title: Incorrect count of tubal rings up to isomorphism
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol correction fixes the count, the classification result survives, and no claim or guarantee depends on the wrong value.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Furthermore, it can be verified that weak inverses for non-zero elements are given by:

issues.failure_explanation:
The first formula requires $a^2 
eq b^2$, not merely $a 
eq b$. For $a = -b 
eq 0$ (e.g., the lightlike element $1 - \sj$), the denominator $a^2 - b^2$ vanishes, so neither displayed formula applies, yet the element has a weak inverse: for $z = a(1-\sj)$ one checks $z^\winv = (1-\sj)/(4a)$, i.e., coordinates $(1/(4a), -1/(4a))$, satisfies $z z^\winv z = z$ and $z^\winv z z^\winv = z^\winv$.

failure_location.quote: \begin{bmatrix} a \\ b \end{bmatrix}^\winv = \begin{bmatrix} a/(a^2-b^2) \\ -b/(a^2-b^2)\end{bmatrix}\,\,(\text{for }a\neq b), \quad\quad \begin{bmatrix} a \\ a \end{bmatrix}^\winv = \begin{bmatrix} 1/4a \\ 1/4a \end{bmatrix}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair:
Change the stated condition from $a 
eq b$ to $a^2 
eq b^2$ (equivalently $|a| 
eq |b|$), and note that the case $a = -b 
eq 0$ is covered by the analogue $(1/(4a), -1/(4a))$.
issues.overall_effect: The example's weak-inverse formulas do not cover the case $a=-b\neq0$; the example's conclusion that split-complex numbers form a tubal ring is unaffected since weak inverses exist there too.
issues.title: Split-complex weak-inverse formula stated with wrong validity range
issues.why_classification: The validity range of one displayed formula is misstated; the correction is local, the weak-inverse property itself is correctly established, and the example's conclusion survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Clearly, for any two tubes $\va$ and $\vb$ of the same size $\va \Mgeq \vb$ implies $\Fnorm{\hat{\va}} \geq \Fnorm{\hat{\vb}}$
Also, in each frontal slice, the diagonal elements are non-increasing. This immediately implies the ordering in the theorem statement.

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed implication is false: with $\matM = \matF_2$ (so $c = \sqrt{2}$, $\matW = \matF_2/\sqrt{2}$), take $\va = (-9, 0)^\mathsf{T}$ and $\vb = (-10, 0)^\mathsf{T}$; then $\matM(\va - \vb) = (1, 1)$ is real and elementwise non-negative, so $\va \Mgeq \vb$, but $\Fnorm{\hat{\va}} = 9\sqrt{2} < 10\sqrt{2} = \Fnorm{\hat{\vb}}$. The corollary's conclusion is nevertheless correct because it is applied only to singular tubes $\vsigma_j$, whose transforms $\hat{\vsigma}_j$ are real, entrywise non-negative, and entrywise at least $\hat{\vsigma}_{j+1}$, which does imply $\Fnorm{\hat{\vsigma}_j} \geq \Fnorm{\hat{\vsigma}_{j+1}}$.

failure_location.quote: Clearly, for any two tubes $\va$ and $\vb$ of the same size $\va \Mgeq \vb$ implies $\Fnorm{\hat{\va}} \geq \Fnorm{\hat{\vb}}$, and combined with the equality $\Fnorm{\vsigma_j} = \frac{1}{|c|}\Fnorm{\hat{\vsigma}_j}$ for $j=1,\dots,\min(m,p)$ we get the desired result.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false general implication with the direct argument: $\hat{\vsigma}_j$ is real and entrywise non-negative with $\hat{\vsigma}_j \geq \hat{\vsigma}_{j+1}$ entrywise, hence $\Fnorm{\hat{\vsigma}_j} \geq \Fnorm{\hat{\vsigma}_{j+1}}$, and conclude via $\Fnorm{\vsigma_j} = |c|^{-1} \Fnorm{\hat{\vsigma}_j}$.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary's statement (norm ordering of the singular tubes) remains valid; only the proof's general justification is false and must be replaced by an entrywise argument for singular tubes.
issues.title: False general norm-monotonicity claim used in the proof of the singular-tube ordering
issues.why_classification: The conclusion is correct and the fix is a one-line justification restricted to the objects actually used; no claim, rate, or dependent result is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: From $\FnormS{\hat{\tenB}} = |c|^2 \FnormS{\tenB}$ one obtains $\FnormS{\tenA - \lrapprox{\tenA}{\vr}} = |c|^{-2} \FnormS{\hat{\tenA} - \widehat{\lrapprox{\tenA}{\vr}}} = |c|^{-2} \sum_{j=1}^n \sum_{i=r_j+1}^{\rank(\hat{\matA}_j)} \hat{\sigma}_{ij}^2$, so the factor must be $|c|^{-2}$, not $|c|^{-1}$. This is consistent with the first Eckart-Young theorem, whose error formula $\sum_{i>k} \FnormS{\vsigma_i}$ is correct precisely because $\FnormS{\vsigma_i} = |c|^{-2} \FnormS{\hat{\vsigma}_i}$. As stated, the identity is false whenever $|c| \neq 1$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the factor $|c|^{-1}$ to $|c|^{-2}$ (equivalently, write the error using primal-domain tube norms as in the first Eckart-Young theorem).
issues.overall_effect: Only the error identity of Theorem thm:second-eckart-young is wrong; its main optimality guarantee and the first Eckart-Young theorem are unaffected.
issues.title: Wrong scaling factor in the error identity of the multirank Eckart-Young theorem
issues.why_classification: The correction is a single factor forced by the paper's own scaling computations; the optimality claim and all guarantees survive with no loss of content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let  $\matM\in\C^{n\times n}$ be an invertible matrix. The result of Eq. \eqref{eq:Mprod} is real for every $\va,\vb\in \R^n$, if and only if every row of $\matM$ is either real, or is conjugate to exactly one other row of $\matM$.

issues.failure_explanation: As stated, the claim is false: take $\matW = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\begin{bmatrix} 1 & \si \\ \si & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ (unitary), $\matD = \diag(2, 3)$, and $\va = \vx = \y = (1, 0)^\mathsf{T}$; then $\dotprod{\va \Mprod \vx}{\y} = \frac{2 + 3\si}{2\sqrt{2}}$ while $\dotprod{\vx}{\va^\sconj \Mprod \y} = \frac{2 - 3\si}{2\sqrt{2}}$ (and $\va^\sconj = (0, -\si)$ is not even real). The missing hypothesis is that the $\Mprod$ product be real — equivalently, every row of $\matM$ is real or is the entry-wise conjugate of exactly one other row (Lemma lem:added-14); the proof silently needs this to replace the transpose by the conjugate transpose. With that hypothesis the identity does hold, since the correct expansion is $\vx^\ha \matW^\ha \matD \diag(\overline{\matW}\va) \matW \y$ and $\matD$ commutes with the diagonal factor. Independently, the printed adjoint expansion $(\matW^\ha \diag(\matW\va) \matD \matW \vx)^\ha = \vx^\ha \matD \matW^\ha \diag(\matW\va)^\ha \matW \vy$ is wrong (the adjoint reverses the order to $\vx^\ha \matW^\ha \matD \dots$), and the next displayed line swaps the factors back, so the two misprints cancel and the final line is correct.

failure_location.quote: Suppose that $\matM=\matD\matW$ for some invertible real diagonal matrix and unitary $\matW$. Then for every $\va,\vx,\vy$ we have

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that $\matM$ defines a real product (row real-or-conjugate-pair condition of Lemma lem:added-14); then the identity holds, and the proof goes through after correcting the adjoint expansion to $\vx^\ha \matW^\ha \matD \diag(\overline{\matW}\va) \matW \y$ and deleting the compensating swap.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition is false for the general class it advertises ($\matM = \matD\matW$ without a realness condition); the Hilbert-algebra interpretation is justified only after adding that hypothesis. The Eckart-Young discussion, which concerns scaled unitary $\matM$ (a subclass for which the identity is true), is not directly harmed.
issues.title: Hilbert-algebra identity stated without the hypothesis that the product is real; proof's adjoint expansion also miscomputed
issues.why_classification: The statement is false as written and needs a substantive structural hypothesis added, and the proof needs a corrected computation; the intended result survives in comparable form, so the loss is limited but more than a local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose that $\matM=\matD\matW$ for some invertible real diagonal matrix and unitary $\matW$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof reduces the identity to the per-tube identity $\dotprod{\tenA_{ij} \Mprod \matX_{j1:}}{\matY_{i1:}} = \dotprod{\matX_{j1:}}{\tenA_{ij}^\sconj \Mprod \matY_{i1:}}$, which is exactly the identity of Proposition prop:hilbert-algebra and requires $\matM = \matD\matW$ with real product. The proposition states no such hypothesis, and the identity fails for general tubal rings: e.g., the valid tubal matrix $\matM = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & \si & -1 \\ 1 & -\si & -1 \end{bmatrix}$ ($n = 3$; row one real, rows two and three exact conjugates, $\det = -4\si \neq 0$) is not of the form $\matD\matW$ — $(\matM\matM^\ha)_{12} = -\si \neq 0$ whereas $\matD\matW(\matD\matW)^\ha = \matD^2$ would be diagonal — and the per-tube identity fails already for $\va = \ve_2$, where the condition $\matM^\mathsf{T} \diag(\matM\va) \matM^{-\mathsf{T}} = \matM^{-1} \diag(\overline{\matM}\va) \matM$ gives $(1,2)$ entries $-1$ and $\si$.

failure_location.quote: Suppose that $\tenA\in\KM^{m\times p}$. For every $\matX \in \KM^p$ and $\matY\in\KM^m$ we have $\dotprod{\tenA \Mprod \matX}{\matY} = \dotprod{\matX}{\tenA^{\ha} \Mprod \matY}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that $\matM = \matD\matW$ with real product (or restrict to the class of the repaired Proposition prop:hilbert-algebra); the proof then follows by summing the per-tube identity over the entries.
issues.overall_effect: The tensor adjoint identity is false for general tubal rings; it holds only under the added hypothesis (scaled-unitary-type $\matM$ with real product), which is the class relevant to the Eckart-Young discussion.
issues.title: Tensor-level adjoint identity stated for all tubal rings without the hypothesis needed for the per-tube identity
issues.why_classification: The statement as written is false for valid tubal rings outside the $\matD\matW$ class (concrete counterexample); the repair adds a substantive hypothesis that shrinks the advertised scope from all tubal rings to a comparable subclass, so more than a minor local fix is needed, though the intended result survives.
